title: Millenburg camp picnics and lawn parties
summary: He describes Sunday picnic trains to Milneburg camps, pay of a dollar and a half or so, and lawn parties with gumbo, in the yard or house.

blocks.x: Tranchino's. Tranchino's. I played that too already, but I know that too. Hey, Ron played that. Huh? Hey, Ron. Peter on Peter, that's right. Oh, God, I only called him this club. What used to happen out at Millenburg? Huh? What used to happen out at Millenburg? I never was there. What used to happen? Well, they had plenty of camps out there. I played out there regularly. You know, so many job differences. They get picnics at camps out there, paper white, paper colored. And every Sunday, 9 o'clock train, 15 cents round trip. We had a 69 o'clock picnic. So everybody was leaving the fee left for picnics. Two and a half, two and a quarter, two dollars. And all day picnics. You all had all you wanted to eat and drink. Have good time. Did you ever play lawn parties? Lawn parties? Oh, that's me, right? Tell us about it. We never saw one. Huh? Tell us a little. How was a lawn party? A lawn party? What was it like? I never seen one. You never seen one where you were, huh? But you never seen one. I went to a lawn party and that, but they sell you to have a band and drink, eat, dance. That's all. Whiskey, you know. Gombo. You eat Gombo? I love it. I love it. I eat it every day since I came here.
The lawn party was right outdoors. You eat red beans? Oh, yeah.

I can cook them too. Yeah, I don't eat them. I don't eat no kind of beans. No? No. Well, I'll tell you. Used to get a dollar and a half, a dollar and sixty-two dollars, a dime two and a half, a man, you know. It's coming with the people you play for. It was the people you play for. It was the people you play for. It was the people you play for. It was good time. That's called it. They had one of my friends at the camp out there, Lucian. Lucian, what's his name again? What? What? Where's that camp out there? Camp out where?

You always have that in your hospital, you always have anything? You don't know what you're doing. I don't know you don't. I don't believe you know me. But you're not that common man. There's the lawn parties.
Did they dance outdoors? Lawn parties.

Lawn parties. Lawn parties. Is this your party or whatever you got- Outdoors? No, in your house or in the hall, in the way you want to give it. You can give it to your house. You understand? I suppose I feel like giving a party. You get a band and get them out, and a white, you know, and cook, and bombo, and chicken. But didn't you play outdoors sometimes? Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. Lawn parties. Play in the yard, yes. That's what I'm talking about. Oh, you mean lawn parties. Yes. That's right. I know what you're talking about now. It's good weather though. But it's not bad weather. Well, they give it in the house. You can do it in the house. But it's so hot now. Lawn parties. Yeah. Lawn parties. Man, I feel like that kind of party.
